description: The title announces a document genre followed by its parent — "Review for: <replication paper>", "Review of: …", "Decision Revise: …", "Recommendation of: …", "Correction to: …" — so the record is the editorial artifact and not the study it names. These objects echo the paper's title verbatim, which is why they carry replication phrases at all. The pattern is START-ANCHORED on purpose, and that anchor is the whole rule: it fires on a title that says what the object IS and never on a paper that discusses the genre. The alternation has two halves for one reason: a genre name that runs on into its parent ("Review for Nature: …") ends at a word boundary, while the forms PCI Registered Reports, Qeios and Copernicus mint separate the genre from the parent with a colon, and `\b` cannot match after one. The colon is therefore REQUIRED on those arms, which is what keeps `^review of` from firing on an article titled "Review of replication practice in psychology". For the same reason there is deliberately NO bare `^editorial` arm — an article titled "Editorial independence and the replication of published findings" is a paper, and that alternative would break the genre-plus-parent property the pattern rests on. OPEN SCOPE QUESTION (D2): `correction to` and `author response` objects sometimes contain a substantive failed reproduction. Both have been in the pattern since it was ported; whether they should be is a definition question for FLoRA, not a fact about the pattern. A SECOND SCOPE QUESTION (issue #192) the pattern cannot reach: a PCI RR recommendation record carries the recommended paper's OWN title, with no genre prefix, so nothing here fires on it. Whether such a record belongs in FLoRA, or should be deduplicated against the paper it recommends, is a definition question too. Above admission (`replication-claim`, 700): the artifact echoes its parent's title, so the replication phrases it carries are its parent's, not its own.

match.title_regex: ^\s*(?:(?:review for|decision letter for|peer review #|faculty opinions recommendation of|correction to|author response)\b|(?:review of|recommendation of|decision (?:revise|reject|accept))\s*:)

measured.rationale: Carried verbatim from the retired `editorial-artifact` spec, which ported it from SciMeto's NON_SCHOLARLY_REPLICATION_CONTEXTS; in production in keyword_verdict() since Stage 2 existed. A record titled 'Decision letter for: <replication paper>' is definitionally not the study, so no sample is needed: the claim is about what the start-anchored genre name means, not about a rate. The precedence changed in the v2 rewrite (555 -> 955) because the rule belongs with the definitional discards that outrank admission; the pattern did not change.

The colon-separated arms (`review of:`, `recommendation of:`, `decision revise|reject|accept:`). Count over a named population: 652 of the 5,146,160 works in the survivor pool match them, and none of those 652 matches the word-boundary arms, so the two halves do not overlap. 25 of the 652 drawn at random and read: all 25 are review or decision objects — Qeios reviews (10.32388), PCI reviews and decision letters (10.24072), one Copernicus referee comment (10.5194/…-rc2) — and none is a study. Recall against data/flora.csv is exact and unchanged: the colon arms match 0 of its 2,504 titles (the one FLoRA title these patterns reach, 'Correction to Gerber and Green (2000)…', is matched by the `correction to` arm and belongs to open question D2). 19 rows of the 2,335-row 2026-08 extracted.csv were review and decision objects reaching Stage 3 as replications, up to six per replicated paper; the colon arms match all 19.
